_comment: Contract §5 / §3 — the degraded ladder, one isolated freshly-seeded store per case. seedMutation says how to doctor the loaded state (data, not code). get.value for 'default' outcomes is the NODE-LANE answer (the graph surface every engine promises); warn counts and latch/reset postures are per-engine (§9 entry 1) and pinned in-engine. excluded: {engine: reason} marks a sanctioned §9 divergence — the engine named skips the case as data (visited, counted, logged). GENERATED by src/__tests__/runtime/character-contract-fixtures.test.ts (inputs: the real JSON export; expectations: the HTML runtime) — do not hand-edit; regenerate with REGEN_FIXTURES=1 and re-copy into the three plugin repos.

cases.description: An id no index entry carries, with NO path sibling: the boolean arm answers its type default and the write is refused. Warn posture and latch/reset semantics are per-engine (§9 entry 1) and pinned in-engine, not here.

An id no index entry carries, with NO path sibling: the integer arm answers its type default and the write is refused. Warn posture and latch/reset semantics are per-engine (§9 entry 1) and pinned in-engine, not here.

An id no index entry carries, with NO path sibling: the float arm answers its type default and the write is refused. Warn posture and latch/reset semantics are per-engine (§9 entry 1) and pinned in-engine, not here.

An id no index entry carries, with NO path sibling: the map arm answers its type default and the write is refused. Warn posture and latch/reset semantics are per-engine (§9 entry 1) and pinned in-engine, not here.

A dangling id whose node still carries the wire path sibling: §3 mandates falling back to the path field, so both halves land on the villain. Engines warn once in the character vocabulary (A6(b)); the internal shape of the fall-through is §9 entry 2 (behaviorally equivalent three ways).
cases.note: Reference lane: the path (the HTML embed never ships a stale id/path pair, so the reference's fall-back IS its path lane).

cases.description: An index entry whose record key matches NO loaded record: resolution is a whole miss (default + refusal). Construct it from the `ghost` field: inject that index/bridge entry before running.

The same rung reached through the SAVE lane: a save whose characters section lacks the record is applied wholesale, leaving a bridged id with no record. Unreal-only: merge-load engines never remove a record at save apply (§9 entry 3), so for them this variant is unreachable and the ghost-index case above is the rung's only door.

excluded.unity: §9 entry 3: save apply MERGES per-variable and never removes a record; the unloaded rung is ghost-index-only in this engine.
excluded.godot: §9 entry 3: save apply MERGES per-variable and never removes a record; the unloaded rung is ghost-index-only in this engine.

cases.description: A pre-P4 export: no character-index.json, no id fields — bare paths keep resolving and writing exactly as before (§5 back-compat pin). The bridge is simply empty; nothing warns.

A name the record does not declare: the read answers the type default (A6(d): the ById default parameter covers RESOLUTION misses only — this stays the surface's own miss posture), and the write is a silent no-op that NEVER creates the variable (A3(b)).
cases.postCondition: the record declares exactly as many variables after the write as before

cases.description: A write whose declared type does not match the node snapshot: refused, nothing lands. (Type-mismatched READ coercion is deliberately NOT pinned cross-engine — only the write refusal is contract.)

A character wired onto the accessor pin overrides the node binding BEFORE the id is even considered: the dangling id is never consulted and never warns (a wired-over dangling id is healthy, not degraded).
The same wire on the Set side: the write lands on the WIRED character, not on the dangling binding.
No id, no path, no wire: the read answers the type default and the write is refused.
